best_for: Windows users who type the same phrases, click the same buttons or remap the same keys every day, and who are willing to write a few lines of script to stop doing it by hand.
description:
AutoHotkey is a scripting tool for Windows, published by AutoHotkey Foundation LLC. Its manual credits Steve Gray and Chris Mallett, and names AutoIt v2, which Jonathan Bennett released as free software in 1999, as the project that inspired it.

Besides keyboard and mouse shortcuts, a hotkey can also be a button on a game controller. A script can start programs, find a window and move, resize or close it, and Window Spy tells you a window's name and controls. You can build your own small windows with buttons, text boxes, check boxes, sliders and lists, for a data entry form or a tiny app. Regular expressions handle text, DllCall reaches into Windows itself, and an interactive debugger helps you find mistakes.

points.title: Hotkeys, hotstrings and macros
points.text: AutoHotkey is a scripting language for automating Windows. Typical jobs are remapping keys and mouse buttons, expanding short abbreviations into full text, filling forms and clicking through repetitive steps. A one-line script can save a daily chore.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: AutoHotkey is free and open source under the GNU GPLv2. There is no paid edition.

points.title: v2 is not a drop-in for v1 scripts
points.text: Version 2 removed and changed many commands, including label-based hotkeys. The docs point to the AHK v2 Script Converter for moving old scripts across. The installer can keep v1 and v2 side by side and picks the right one from a script's `#Requires` line.

points.title: Install for yourself or for everyone
points.text: The default install goes into Program Files for all users, which some features such as UI Access need. A current-user install in your local app data folder works without admin rights. `AutoHotkey.exe` alone can also run scripts with no install at all.

points.title: Expect antivirus warnings
points.text: Scripts can be compiled into a standalone .exe with Ahk2Exe. Antivirus tools sometimes flag AutoHotkey or compiled scripts, and the FAQ says these are mostly false positives, more so for compressed builds.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no macOS or Linux version. The Windows listing keeps 48 versions, each with 32-bit and 64-bit installers for either the current user or the whole machine.
